author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Flycast brings per-pixel sorting to OpenGL ES 3.1
summary: The libretro OpenGL ES path can now request the GLES 3.1 context and verify the image atomics, shader-storage blocks, counters, bindings, and buffer limits required by Flycast’s order-independent transparency renderer.
heroAlt: Sega Dreamcast console beside its graphics processor package.

blocks.text: A conventional depth buffer keeps the nearest opaque surface, but overlapping translucent polygons may need several fragments blended in depth order. Flycast’s OIT renderer uses a per-pixel linked-list approach so fragments can be collected and resolved after the draw rather than relying on a single fixed layer. Each pixel records a head pointer into a shared fragment buffer, while atomics allocate nodes safely across parallel fragment invocations.
GLES 3.1 exposes the required building blocks

The merged change asks libretro frontends for an explicit OpenGL ES 3.1 context when the OIT renderer is selected. It adds the image-atomic and shader-storage support used by the renderer, requests the context version directly, and uses the appropriate storage-buffer memory barriers for the resolve work. This avoids relying on a frontend to silently return a newer context than the one it was asked to provide.
Check actual limits instead of trusting a version string

A nominal API version does not guarantee enough resources for this renderer. Flycast now checks fragment shader-storage blocks, image units, atomic counters and bindings, combined shader outputs, and storage-buffer sizes. It also handles the GLES image-atomic extension requirement before advertising per-pixel sorting support. If any resource is insufficient, the renderer logs which capability failed rather than attempting the path blindly.

The patch also retains framebuffer readback buffers rather than allocating fresh storage on every frame. That change reduces repeated allocation work in the same rendering path. The feature therefore depends on both correct GPU capability detection and careful synchronization between fragment writes and the later compositing pass. Testing should include GLES implementations at the minimum supported version and verify both transparent ordering and unsupported-device fallback behavior.
